title: Regional routing circuit-breaker and warm-priming readiness orchestration
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a circuit-breaker driven regional routing controller that coordinates warm-standby priming and a quantitative readiness score for each standby candidate. This ticket covers design and implementation of the orchestration logic, readiness probes, fallback model-variant selection, rollout gating, and acceptance tests.

Background: We already route by geo priority and have warm caches in some regions, but outages and sudden capacity pressure can cause noisy failovers and long tail latency. Current behavior lacks a single readiness gate combining capacity headroom, KV cache warmth, and model-latency tail behavior; teams end up doing ad-hoc throttles or manual rollbacks.

Proposed solution:
- Readiness score: calculate a per-region readiness score (0-100) composed of: capacity_headroom_pct (weight 35%), kv_cache_hit_ratio_recent (25%), p95_model_latency_ms normalized (25%), and recent error-rate (15%). Thresholds: readiness >= 70 => eligible for routing; 50-70 => degraded with limited traffic; <50 => ineligible.
- Circuit breaker rules: automatic partial-shed when p95 > configured threshold (default 300ms) OR capacity_headroom < 12% OR error-rate spike > 2x baseline in last 5m. Circuit-breaker enters a cooldown with exponential backoff and notifies console.
- Warm-priming protocol for standby region activation: on eligibility change from ineligible->eligible initiate warm-priming run: 1) prefetch top-1k prefixes from heatmap (last 72h) into KV cache, 2) populate model token cache with representative front-loaded prompts using synthetic shadow traffic, 3) run 10-minute shadow traffic at 5-10% of production QPS for smoke validation. Warm-priming has instrumentation: prefetch success ratio, KV hit ratio delta, model-tail-latency trend.
- Fallback model-variant mapping: policy file maps primary models to compatible fallback families and degradation tiers (primary -> quantized-int8 -> small-fp16 -> micro). Selection is based on compatibility metadata (vocab, layer mapping) and runtime cost profile. Controller should prefer warm-warmed variants.
- Routing policy integration: Smart router will consult readiness scores and circuit-breaker state when making decisions. Policy combinators: region_priority, tier_preference, and fallback_variant_preference.
- Observability and runbooks: add console widgets for readiness score components and a playbook for manual override and rollback. Add automatic incident annotations when circuit-breaker trips.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design data model and operator APIs (CRDs/internal store) for readiness scores and circuit-breaker state.
2) Instrument metrics: capacity headroom, kv_prefetch_success, kv_hit_ratio_1m/5m, p95/p99 latency per model-variant, recent error-rate.
3) Add warm-priming worker that can run prefetch and shadow traffic jobs; waveform control for adjustable QPS.
4) Implement controller logic that computes readiness and emits events. Expose API for the router to query readiness via gRPC and cache.
5) Implement fallback selection using compatibility table and cost heuristics (config-driven).
6) Write integration tests and chaos scenarios (regional outage, cold-cache, model-variant OOM).
7) Rollout: stage in dev->canary->prod. Canary will enable routing to candidate region for mirrored traffic first then shift 5% traffic for 1 hour, then ramp using SLO-preserving algorithm.

Acceptance criteria:
- Readiness score computed and visible for all regions in prod-telemetry within 24h of deploy.
- Warm-priming job can complete prefetch of top-1k prefixes in <5m for a standard region and raise KV hit ratio by >=20 percentage points over baseline on test traffic.
- Circuit-breaker trips automatically under simulated p95 spike and prevents routing to impacted region.
- Fallback model variants selected according to policy, verified via unit tests and integration run where primary is intentionally evicted.
- End-to-end failover simulation shows tail latency degradation <20% compared to steady-state and no more than 90s of increased 95th latency during cutover in staged tests.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Routing+Readiness (work in progress)
- Heatmap service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/heatmap/pull/182
- Warm-priming worker initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priming/pull/23

Notes: Controllers should be resilient to partial metric loss; missing data counts as conservative (reduces readiness). We should avoid global coordination for every request; router should poll readiness cache with TTL 30s. Decisioning must be idempotent and tolerant of transient flaps.
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with infra, serving-runtime, and router teams. Agreed on composite readiness score and weightings. Action: Marco to prototype readiness calculator and heatmap prefetch API.

2026-03-03: Prototype readiness calculator implemented (branch: feat/readiness-score). Initial simulated scores look reasonable against replayed traffic. Keeping weights configurable via feature-flag.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and SRE. PM requested explicit canary ramp steps and customer-impact annotation. SRE asked for circuit-breaker cooldown policy to be configurable per-customer for Dedicated deployments.

2026-03-07: Warm-priming worker MVP completed. Prefetch task runs but needs throttling to avoid bursty backend load. Added token-bucket limiter in worker; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priming/pull/23

2026-03-09: Integration test plan added to repo under infra/tests/readiness. Next: run chaos sim for regional outage and verify router respects readiness cache. Assigned to: Marco Silva and Lina Park.
2026-03-11: Security flagged that fallback variant selection must preserve model signing verification for private deployments. Added to dependencies; security review scheduled.

2026-03-12: Ran local chaos sim: evicted primary region, readiness dropped below 50 for 3rd-party region, circuit-breaker tripped and routing shifted to fallback region successfully. Observed KV prefetch improved hit ratio by 27% over baseline. Will iterate on threshold tuning before canary.
